([[Suffield, Connecticut]]) | college = *[[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale]] (2016–2019) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = *[[Ivy League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Ivy League Player of the Year]] (2019) *2× First-team All-[[Ivy League]] (2018, 2019) *Second-team All-Ivy League (2017) }} '''Olumiye "Miye" Oni'''{{cite web |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=How Yale's Miye Oni Went From Division 3 College Commit to An NBA Prospect |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/adamzagoria/2019/01/07/how-yales-miye-oni-went-from-division-3-college-commit-to-an-nba-prospect/#5d1d456f1a92 |website=[[Forbes]] |accessdate=March 12, 2019 |date=January 7, 2019}} (born August 4, 1997) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale Bulldogs]]. Listed at {{height|ft=6|in=6}} and 210 pounds (129 kg), he plays the [[shooting guard]] position. Oni was named [[Ivy League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Ivy League Player of the Year]] in 2019 and is a three-time All-Ivy League selection. He has often been projected as a potential selection at the [[2019 NBA draft]] as a rare prospect from the Ivy League. Measured 6’4.25” at the NBA Pre-Draft Combine. Oni, who is of Nigerian descent, grew up in [[Northridge, Los Angeles]] and began playing high school basketball at [[Viewpoint School]], where he was named the divisional player of the year. He was lightly recruited at Viewpoint and committed to [[Williams College]] of the [[NCAA Division III]]. After drawing more interest as a senior at Viewpoint, he committed to Yale, but admissions rules forced him to play an additional season of prep basketball at [[Suffield Academy]] before college. ==Early life== Oni was born to Nigerian parents Opeyemi and Oludotun Oni. His father is a professor at the [[University of Phoenix]] and an engineer. Oni began playing basketball at age two with a toy hoop and joined a [[YMCA]] league with his older sister at age five.{{cite web |last1=Kent |first1=Richard |title=Q&A with Oludotun Oni, father of Miye Oni |url=http://ivyhoopsonline.com/2019/03/01/qa-with-oludotun-oni-father-of-miye-oni/ |publisher=Ivy Hoops Online |accessdate=March 12, 2019 |date=March 1, 2019}} From a young age, he had aspirations to play in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and admired [[Kobe Bryant]] of the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web |last1=Belli |first1=Brita |title=Heading into “Ivy Madness,” all eyes on NBA prospect Miye Oni |url=https://news.yale.edu/2019/03/14/heading-ivy-madness-all-eyes-nba-prospect-miye-oni |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 18, 2019 |date=March 14, 2019}} In addition to basketball, he played [[American football|football]], mainly as a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] and [[wide receiver]], and [[baseball]]. ==High school career== Oni started playing high school basketball at [[Viewpoint School]] in [[Calabasas, California]] under head coach J. J. Prince. He played for the [[junior varsity team]] in his freshman season, when he stood {{convert|5|ft|9|in|m|2}} and weighed {{convert|140|lbs|kg|0}}.{{cite web |last1=Fattal |first1=Tarek |title=Former Viewpoint basketball player Miye Oni emerging as first-round NBA prospect |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/01/05/former-viewpoint-basketball-player-miye-oni-emerging-as-first-round-nba-prospect/ |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |accessdate=March 12, 2019 |date=January 5, 2019}} As a junior, Oni suffered a knee injury that sidelined him for most of the season.{{cite web |last1=Jacobs |first1=Jeff |title=The NBA may be in his future, but Miye Oni is relishing a special season at Yale |url=https://www.ctpost.com/sports/jeffjacobs/article/Jeff-Jacobs-The-NBA-may-be-in-his-future-but-13527849.php |website=[[Connecticut Post]] |accessdate=March 12, 2019 |date=January 11, 2019}} The injury hindered his [[college recruiting]] because he did not have film to show college coaches before his senior year. Oni stood {{convert|6|ft|4|in|m|2}} and weighed {{convert|180|lbs|kg|0}} by the time he was a senior. He had a breakout final season for Viewpoint, averaging 18 points, 9 rebounds, and 4 assists and being named [[California Interscholastic Federation]] (CIF) Division 5AA player of the year.{{cite web |title=Miye Oni |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2017-18/bios/oni_miye_npi2 |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 12, 2019}} At Viewpoint, Oni did not draw interest from [[NCAA Division I]] basketball programs and was only recruited by [[NCAA Division III|Division III]] school [[Williams College]], where he committed in the fall of his senior year of high school. However, Williams did not offer enough [[student financial aid (United States)|financial aid]] for his family to meet the cost of attendance. During his senior season at Viewpoint, Oni attracted attention from [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale]] assistant coach Matt Kingsley. After watching his highlight video in the spring of 2015, Yale head coach [[James Jones (basketball coach)|James Jones]] offered him, and Oni committed to play for the team on July 1, 2015.{{cite web |title=Miye Oni |url=http://www.espn.com/collegskee-sports/batball/recruiting/player/_/id/213447/miye-oni |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=March 13, 2019}}. However, since Yale admissions were closed, he spent his next season playing for [[Suffield Academy]], a [[College-preparatory school|prep school]] in [[Suffield, Connecticut]], located near [[Yale University]]. With Suffield, Oni averaged 17 points, 6 rebounds and 5 assists and earned [[New England Preparatory School Athletic Council]] (NEPSAC) Class A player of the year distinction. On February 5, 2016, he scored 52 points with 11 three-pointers versus [[Wilbraham & Monson Academy]] at the National Prep School Invitational, breaking his school record and [[Shabazz Napier]]'s tournament record.{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Corey |title=NPSI Day One: Miye Oni scorches the nets |url=https://hoopseen.com/news/general/201602/npsi-day-one-miye-oni-scorches-nets |publisher=HoopSeen |accessdate=March 14, 2019 |date=February 5, 2016}} Oni was named most outstanding player of the event. He was a nominee for the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]].{{cite web |title=2016 McDonald's All American Games Nominees |url=https://www.mcdonaldsallamerican.com/content/aag/en/MediaCenter/2016/2016-game-materials/2016-Nominee-List/_jcr_content/featuredcontent/everything/file.res/2016%20Nominee%20List%20%28Boys_Girls%29%20Final%281%29.pdf |publisher=[[McDonald's All-American Game]] |accessdate=March 14, 2019 |date=February 1, 2016}} ==College career== ===Freshman=== Oni made his debut for Yale on November 13, 2016, recording a team-high 24 points, 6 rebounds, and 3 assists in a 98–90 upset win over [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]].{{cite web |title=Bulldogs Stun Washington 98-90 |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2016-17/releases/20161113zmio1n |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 14, 2019 |date=November 13, 2016}} In his next game, he posted 13 points, 10 rebounds, and a season-best 5 blocks in an 89–81 victory over [[Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball|Lehigh]].{{cite web |title=Five Players In Double Figures In 89-81 Win Over Lehigh |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2016-17/releases/20161117yc0h2s |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 14, 2019 |date=November 17, 2016}} Oni claimed [[Ivy League]] Rookie of the Week honors in each of his first three weeks with Yale.{{cite web |title=Miye Oni’s college career with Yale men’s basketball team off to a great start |url=https://www.nhregister.com/colleges/article/Miye-Oni-s-college-career-with-Yale-men-s-11326078.php |website=[[New Haven Register]] |accessdate=March 14, 2019 |date=December 2, 2016}} On February 25, 2017, he scored a season-high 27 points while chipping in 7 rebounds and 4 assists, in a 99–86 win over [[Dartmouth Big Green men's basketball|Dartmouth]].{{cite web |title=Bulldogs One Step Closer To Clinching Berth In Ivy League Tournament |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2016-17/releases/20170225yqupn5 |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 16, 2019 |date=February 25, 2017}} By the end of the season, Oni was averaging 12.9 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 2.7 assists per game.{{cite web |title=Miye Oni Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Miye-Oni/Summary/93804 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=March 16, 2019}} He earned second-team All-Ivy League recognition and was named conference Rookie of the Week on five different occasions during the season.{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball All-Ivy, Postseason Awards Announced |url=http://www.ivyleague.com/sports/mbkb/2016-17/releases/Men-s_Basketball_All-Ivy-_Postseason_Awards_Announced |publisher=[[Ivy League]] |accessdate=March 16, 2019 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170314232228/http://www.ivyleague.com:80/sports/mbkb/2016-17/releases/Men-s_Basketball_All-Ivy-_Postseason_Awards_Announced |archivedate=March 14, 2017 |date=March 8, 2017}} ===Sophomore=== Entering the [[2017–18 Yale Bulldogs men's basketball team|2017–18 season]], the ''[[Hartford Courant]]'' speculated that the Yale duo of Oni and [[Makai Mason]] could be "one of the top backcourts in the country."{{cite web |last1=Conner |first1=Desmond |title=Yale's Oni, Mason, Could Be One Of Best Backcourts In 2017-18 |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/college/hc-sp-yale-basketball-feature-20171012-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |accessdate=March 16, 2019 |date=October 13, 2017}} On November 14, 2017, his third appearance in his sophomore season, he led all scorers with 20 points in an 86–54 victory over [[South Carolina State Bulldogs men's basketball|South Carolina State]].{{cite web |title=Bulldogs Roll Over South Carolina State 86-54 |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2017-18/releases/20171114xxxgje |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 16, 2019 |date=November 14, 2017}} Oni erupted for 26 points, his best mark in the season, and recorded team-highs of 7 rebounds and 4 assists on November 25, in a 79–73 loss to [[Vermont Catamounts men's basketball|Vermont]].{{cite web |title=Vermont Holds Off Yale 79-73 |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2017-18/releases/20171125qxdeob |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 16, 2019 |date=November 25, 2017}} On February 24, 2018, he flirted with a [[double (basketball)|triple-double]] in an 83–73 win over [[Columbia Lions men's basketball|Columbia]], matching his season-high of 26 points while leading his team with 9 rebounds and 8 assists.{{cite web |title=Bulldogs Punch Ticket To Ivy League Tournament, Knock Off Columbia 83-73 |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2017-18/releases/201802250qm0k1 |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 17, 2019 |date=February 24, 2018}} Through 29 games, Oni averaged 15.1 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 3.6 assists per game, leading Yale in all three categories. He tied the school record for three-pointers attempted in a single season, with 184.{{cite web |title=Team & Individual Records |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2011-12/files/records_web.pdf |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 19, 2019}} Oni was a three-time Ivy League Player of the Week, unanimous first-team All-Ivy League pick, and [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] (NABC) District 13 second-team selection. ===Junior=== [[File:Miye Oni (cropped 2).jpg|thumb|Oni (right) skies for a block in December 2018.]] Oni made his junior season debut on November 9, 2018, scoring 16 points in a 76–59 win over [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]] at the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] China Game held in [[Shanghai]].{{cite web |title=Oni, Swain Pace Yale With 16 Points |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/201811105b3j5v |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 18, 2019 |date=November 9, 2018}} On November 21, he posted his first double-double of the season, leading his team with 18 points and 10 rebounds in a 79–70 loss to Vermont.{{cite web |title=Vermont Edges Yale 79-70 |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/20181121varlkf |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 18, 2019 |date=November 21, 2018}} On December 1, Oni scored 29 points and was named game MVP in a 77–73 victory over [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]] at the Hoophall Miami Invitational.{{cite web |title=Miye Oni leads Yale's 2nd-half rally past Miami, 77-73 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/12/01/miye-oni-leads-yales-2nd-half-rally-past-miami-77-73/38655555/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=March 18, 2019 |date=December 1, 2018}}{{cite web |title=Oni Scores 29 Points, Named Game MVP |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/20181201xdue15 |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 18, 2019 |date=December 1, 2018}} He erupted for 31 points, 9 rebounds, and 4 assists, leading his team in each category, on February 2, 2019 in an 89–68 win over Dartmouth. Oni was the first Yale player to record a 30-point game since Anthony Dallier in 2017.{{cite web |title=Oni Scores 31, Bulldogs Rout Dartmouth |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/20190202y7ihj9 |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 19, 2019 |date=February 2, 2019}} In his next game, a 74–60 victory over [[Princeton Tigers men's basketball|Princeton]], he posted a career-high 35 points, 12 rebounds, and 3 blocks. Oni scored the most single-game points in school history since [[Greg Mangano]] in 2012.{{cite web |title=Oni Scores 35 As Bulldogs Knock Off Princeton 74-60 |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/20190208wgxb3j |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 19, 2019 |date=February 8, 2019}} He delivered another strong performance on March 1, when he scored 30 points—shooting 9-of-11 from the field—to help Yale defeat [[Cornell Big Red men's basketball|Cornell]], 88–65, and clinch a spot in the [[2019 Ivy League Men's Basketball Tournament|2019 Ivy league Tournament]].{{cite web |title=Bulldogs Clinch Spot In IvyMadness, Hammer Cornell 88-65 |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/20190301ws51j9 |publisher=[[Yale University]] |accessdate=March 19, 2019 |date=March 1, 2019}} By the end of the regular season, Oni was averaging a team-best 17.4 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 3.6 assists per game. He was named [[Ivy League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Ivy League Player of the Year]], becoming the third Yale player to win the award.{{cite web |last1=Fuller |first1=Jim |title=Yale’s Miye Oni named Ivy League Player of the Year |url=https://www.nhregister.com/colleges/article/Yale-s-Miye-Oni-named-Ivy-League-Player-of-the-13683367.php |website=[[New Haven Register]] |accessdate=March 19, 2019 |date=March 12, 2019}} In his junior season, Oni frequently attracted attention from NBA scouts, who visited all of his games to see him play.{{cite web |last1=Amore |first1=Don |title=For Yale’s Miye Oni, the story just keeps getting better |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/college/hc-sp-amore-column-yale-miye-oni-20190318-20190318-ggkk7v3hsng7pd5mqe46c32nra-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |accessdate=March 18, 2019 |date=March 18, 2019}} He is considered a top-50 prospect for the [[2019 NBA draft]] and could become the first Ivy League player to be drafted since 1995.
